name: Wheel Studs & Lug Nuts
description: 5 x 120 mm bolt pattern, M14 x 1.5 studs pressed into the hub flanges, 60° conical-seat lug nuts torqued to 190 N·m (140 ft-lb). Race builds fit longer studs for thick race wheels/spacers and open-ended race nuts.

components.name: Wheel studs
components.description: Knurled M14x1.5 studs pressed into each hub flange (5 per hub). Replace any stud that was cross-threaded, over-torqued by an impact gun, or stretched.

raceOptions.name: Extended M14x1.5 press-in race studs (+20–30 mm)
raceOptions.notes: Needed with spacers or thick race-wheel pads; size the knurl to the OEM hub. Many race series require thread engagement ≥ stud diameter (≥ 14 mm, ideally full nut).

raceOptions.name: Screw-in stud conversion (hub drilled & tapped) for quick changes

hardware.torque: Press-fit – pull in with a stud installer, not by over-torquing a lug nut

installNotes: Press studs with hub on a bench (or use a stud puller tool on the car); confirm head fully seated against flange.
Never lubricate studs unless the wheel maker specifies it (torque spec is for clean, dry threads).
inspection: Check threads each wheel change; replace any stud with damaged/stretched threads (nut binds mid-thread).

components.name: Lug nuts
components.description: M14x1.5 lug nuts with 60° conical seat. Race nuts are open-ended (stud passes through for visible engagement), steel, often with captive washers matched to the wheel seat.
components.location: On each stud at the wheel face.

factory.name: GM M14x1.5 lug nut, 60° conical seat (22 mm hex typical)

raceOptions.name: ARP M14x1.5 open-end lug nuts
raceOptions.notes: Match seat type to wheel (60° conical vs ball vs flat with washer).

raceOptions.name: Wheel-maker specific nuts (Forgeline / BBS / Apex)
raceOptions.notes: Apex supplies 60° conical nuts for Camaro fitments.

hardware.torqueSequence: Snug all in a star pattern with the wheel off the ground, lower car, then torque in star pattern in two passes (≈ 50%, then 100%)
hardware.notes: GM 2016–18 table "Wheel nuts 190 N·m"; matches wheel-size and Velgen (140 ft-lb, 6th gen).

installNotes: Re-torque after the first session on new wheels / after each wheel change (seats bed in).
Use a calibrated click wrench for final torque, never an impact gun.
inspection: Torque check at every tire change and before each session; mark nuts with a paint stripe.
